question: The Theosophical Society was started by which of the following social reformers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Theosophical Society was co-founded by **Madame H.P. Blavatsky and Colonel H.S. Olcott** in 1875 in New York.
 
• **Annie Besant** became a prominent leader of the Theosophical Society and played a significant role in its activities.
 
• She joined the Theosophical Society in 1889 and later became its president from 1907 to 1933.
 
• Annie Besant was a notable social reformer, women's rights activist, and supporter of Indian self-rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theosophical Society**

 
 
• The Society's primary objective is to promote universal brotherhood and investigate the hidden mysteries of nature and the divine.
 
• It emphasizes the study of comparative religion, philosophy, and science.
 
• The Theosophical Society has branches worldwide, including a significant presence in India.
 
 
 
• **Annie Besant's Contributions**
 
 
• She was involved in the Indian independence movement and became the first woman president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.
 
• Besant also founded the Central Hindu College, which later became part of Banaras Hindu University.
 
• She was a prolific writer and speaker, advocating for various social and political reforms.
 
 
 
• **Madame H.P. Blavatsky**
 
 
• She was a Russian occultist, philosopher, and co-founder of the Theosophical Society.
 
• Blavatsky's major works include "Isis Unveiled" and "The Secret Doctrine."
 
• Her teachings laid the foundation for modern Theosophy.
 
 
 
• **Colonel H.S. Olcott**
 
 
• He was an American military officer, journalist, and co-founder of the Theosophical Society.
 
• Olcott was deeply involved in the society's organizational activities and its spread in Asia, particularly in India and Ceylon (Sri Lanka).
 
• He worked towards the revival of Buddhism in Ceylon and was a key figure in the establishment of Buddhist schools and institutions.
